This is an estimate only: the text was never delivered or timed, and the rehearsal was a silent read-through, not aloud. Argument: the first interpretation (turning), carried by Jerome on Ezek 18 (PL 25, 180), Chrysostom (Hom. in Matt. 67.3-4), Aquinas (Super Matt. c. 21) and Augustine (Sermo 82.14; Enarr. 24.5; In ep. Ioh. 5.12). It is joined to the third (obedient-son) through Chrysostom (Hom. in Phil. 7), Augustine (Tract. 55.7 and 84.1) and Schuster on the Collect (Sacramentary III, pp. 121-122). From the second (two-peoples) it takes only the literal hearers, Chrysostom's 'as having a hope, if they were willing' and Aquinas's application to clerics and religious. The two-peoples identification is not preached, and the application falls on the baptized. The note lists every join the homily makes that no Father makes. It also lists what is left to the studies: the Jerome/Aquinas difference on lapsed works (the homily makes only the claim both hold), Hilary's reversal, John 10:26 with the Alleluia verse, the Entrance Antiphon, the first Communion antiphon with Augustine's Ezek 18:22 join, and the orations' sacramentary history. Branch limits: Phil 2:6-8 is quoted as what Paul goes on to write after 2:5, not as words the assembly heard, so the homily holds under either form of the second reading. The second Communion antiphon is named as one of the two options. Rights: Scripture is the Douay-Rheims study English, and the speech names it once. The orations are described, not quoted, and no Lectionary or Missal English appears. NPNF and Schuster quotations were re-read at their tracked loci at this stage. Jerome and Aquinas are reported without quotation marks, from the Latin the study prints, which this stage did not re-read. All loci are bound in research/source-bindings.toml. Upstream: no new defect found. The standing advisories (STU-001 to STU-010, RES-008, RES-009, SYN-001 to SYN-004) touch nothing the homily uses. summary: Wrote the homily of the Claude postconciliar Twenty-sixth Sunday in Ordinary Time, Year A (PC-S52-A), 'Afterwards He Went', for an adult parish assembly on 27 September 2026: homily.tex (shared title, properhomily enclosing only the spoken component, terminal note after its page break) and the two declared components. The 1,530-word spoken body preaches the first interpretation (each is judged where he is found; no despair, no resting, no tomorrow promised) joined to the third (the Son who obeyed unto death) through the Gospel, Ezekiel, the psalm, Philippians 2, the Collect, the offering, the second Communion antiphon and the Prayer after Communion. Author proof: 4 pages, clean log, reproducible bytes, and every homily-edition check exits 0. No new evidence-dependent claim, and no upstream file edited.
